member.summary: How a font is found for a letter the first font lacks, and whether it is made bold: as the text box does it (the app asks Avalonia's font manager over the whole chain, as its text layout asks it), so the two pick the same face. Walking the chain in order picked Noto Sans KR for "★" where the box has Noto Sans JP, and on Windows 11 25H2 the system, asked without the UI's language, gave the colour Segoe UI Emoji for "👍" where the box has the plain Segoe UI Symbol. Without it (the command line), the chain is walked and the system asked.

member.summary: A letter's bidirectional class (UAX #9, table 4): strong (L, R, AL), weak (EN, AN, ES, ET, CS, NSM, where a boundary neutral such as a joiner counts as NSM) and neutral (whitespace and other neutrals together).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.Levels(System.Text.Rune[],System.Boolean)
member.summary: Each letter's embedding level, 0 to 2, by the rules of UAX #9 for a paragraph without explicit embeddings: W1–W7 for weak types, N1–N2 for neutrals, I1–I2 for levels. A number after Arabic letters is an Arabic number, which takes no sign or percent (W2, W5), so "خصم 50%" shows "%50" on the left as the text box does.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.PairBrackets(System.Text.Rune[],Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.Kind[],Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.Kind[],Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.Kind)
member.summary: N0: a pair of brackets goes the paragraph's way when there is a strong letter of that way inside it; else the other way when there is one of that inside and before it too; else as N1 makes it. So "מחיר (USD) 5" keeps "(USD)" whole, as the text box does. Marks after a bracket go as the bracket.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.Brackets

member.summary: With the app's fallback, as Avalonia's text layout picks it: the first font if it has the letter, else the font before it if that has it, else the one the fallback finds. Without: the first font of the chain that has the letter, else the one before it, else one the system finds.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Annotations.LabelText.SystemPrimary
member.summary: The system's bold font, unless that is a serif or monospaced one (DejaVu Serif on Linux, where Skia's build here can't ask for "sans-serif"); then the first common sans-serif family installed.

Skia's Linux build here finds fonts by family name but never by letter (MatchCharacter returns null even with a Korean font installed), so the installed families are looked through for one that has it, sans-serif ones first.

member.remarks: Rendering draws model space as seen from the top (the active layout when model space is empty), fitted to the page: PDF on an A3 sheet (A4 / Letter when the preset says so), SVG and images with the drawing's aspect ratio on a white background. member.name: T:Filee.Engines.Cad.CadPalette
member.summary: Maps the drawing's colours to the colours printed, like a plot style table in AutoCAD.

remarks.para: Ink is everything drawn with a pen: lines, curves, text, dimensions, hatch pattern lines, points and the small fills that are part of a line (arrowheads, SOLID / TRACE, wide polyline segments). Black and white prints all of it black, as monochrome.ctb does. Grayscale prints it as the gray of its brightness, scaled so the lightest colour is still a mid gray: yellow (the brightest pen colour) would otherwise be almost white, as unreadable as it is now.

Areas are filled hatches (solid, gradient, and the tint of a pattern too dense to draw). monochrome.ctb fills them black, which turns a light background colour into a black block hiding the lines and text drawn over it. Both choices print an area as the gray of its brightness instead: a yellow or light blue fill stays light, a dark fill stays dark, a black one stays black. The page itself stays white.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Data.CsvData.JsonNumber
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match '-' atomically, optionally.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match '0'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [1-9].
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] greedily any number of times.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [+-] atomically, optionally.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Ebooks.CalibreConverter.StallTimeout
member.summary: ebook-convert prints its progress ("34% Running transforms on e-book...") as it works, so a book takes as long as it needs: a 300 MB CHM made into a PDF passed the former fixed 10 minutes (#651). Only this long without a single line means calibre is stuck. As long as that limit was, so no conversion that finished before stops now.

Ranked above the HWPX writer, calibre costs at most 23 + 8 and the built-in route at least 32 (the HWPX writer moves down to + 9).

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Geo.GeoXml.MaxElements
member.summary: How many elements a KML or GPX file may hold. Each costs about 100 bytes in the tree whatever its size, so a file of tiny elements ("<a/>" repeated) would use 25 bytes of memory per character: 40 million characters in a 150 KB KMZ took 1.1 GB. Real files hold a few elements per feature; this allows a million features.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Geo.GeoXml.Load(System.IO.Stream,System.Int32)
member.summary: Parses XML without DTDs or external entities, so a hostile file can't read files or expand into gigabytes, and refuses elements nested more than levels. The tree is built here from the reader rather than by XDocument.Load, which takes time quadratic in the depth (a 1.4 MB file nested 100,000 deep kept it busy for 48 seconds, the reader alone needs a quarter of a second) and so couldn't be allowed to see such a file. Namespace declarations and prefixes are not kept; names are the local name and namespace.

member.remarks:
Pattern:
/\\*.*?\\*/
Options:
RegexOptions.Singleline
Explanation:

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.Hwpx.CssStyleSheet.SimpleSelector
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(\\*|[A-Za-z][\\w-]*)?(\\.[\\w-]+)*$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match '*'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Za-z].
○ Match a character in the set [-\w] greedily any number of times.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [-\w] atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Hwp.Hwpx.HtmlReader.MinDefaultContrast
member.summary: Text with no colour of its own is black because nobody chose it (the page colour is not kept), so it needs a higher contrast than text the page coloured: black stays on #1f2937 at 1.5 only because the style sheet's white body colour was dropped.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Hwp.Hwpx.HtmlReader.MinCodeContrast
member.summary: Code always gets the light , also when a dark highlight theme drew it on a dark background. That theme's token colours were picked for the dark background and show at 1.3 to 2.9 on the code shade (Atom One Dark, VS Code Dark+), above but pale. Light themes' tokens (GitHub, Bootstrap's pink code) stay above 3 and keep their colours.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.Hwpx.HtmlReader.Readable(Filee.Engines.Hwp.Hwpx.HCharFormat,System.String)
member.summary: Keeps text readable when a style sheet only half describes a dark or light page: the page background is not kept (see ), so "color: #fff" can end up on white paper and a dark card ("background: #111827") under the default black text. When the text colour (black if none) and what is behind it (the shade, else the fill of the table cell, else white paper) are too close, the background stays and the text becomes black or white, whichever shows on it.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.RhwpInput.GroupFloatingHeaderPictures(System.Xml.Linq.XDocument)
member.summary: rhwp lays out a floating picture in a header or footer as if it took up room: what comes after it moves down, or is left out past the end of the area (issue #1152). The text beside it and any shapes are not drawn at all, and a position on the paper is taken from the header's corner. As the one object of a group, the picture goes the way of a shape, which has none of this. Only paragraphs without stored lines (written by Filee): for a file saved by 한글 rhwp's reading of the position stays. A paragraph without text keeps its line with a space. True when something changed.

member.summary: In table cells: moves the stored line of a paragraph that holds nothing but one floating table (vertRelTo="PARA", top aligned, text above and below) from under the table up to the paragraph's top. Only when the line is where 한글 puts it, below the table. True when something changed.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.RhwpInput.SpaceEquationLines(System.Xml.Linq.XDocument,System.Xml.Linq.XDocument)
member.summary: Paragraphs without stored lines (written by Filee) that hold equations: room above and below for what rhwp draws outside the line. rhwp makes a line as tall as its tallest equation, puts the line's baseline at 85 % of that height and the equation's own baseline on it, so an equation whose baseline is higher (a fraction, a matrix, a sum with limits) reaches below the line into the next one. The paragraph gets that much more space after it (and before it, for an equation reaching above). True when something changed.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.UnhwpLineBreaks.AtxHeading
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^#{1,6}(?:[ \\t]|$)
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match '#' atomically at least 1 and at most 6 times.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.UnhwpLineBreaks.OrderedListMarker
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^\\d{1,9}[.)](?=[ \\t]|$)
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least 1 and at most 9 times.
○ Match a character in the set [).].
○ Zero-width positive lookahead.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Hwp.UnhwpLineBreaks.BlockStart
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(?:#{1,6}(?:[ \\t]|$)|[-+*](?:[ \\t]|$)|>|`{3}|~{3}|=+[ \\t]*$|-+[ \\t]*$|([*_])[ \\t]*(?:\\1[ \\t]*){2,}$|<[A-Za-z/!?]|:(?:[ \\t]|$)|\\^\\^)
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match with 11 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '#' atomically at least 1 and at most 6 times.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [*+-].
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match '>'.
○ Match the string "```".
○ Match the string "~~~".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '=' atomically at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '-' atomically at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [*_].
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] greedily any number of times.
○ Loop greedily at least twice.
○ Match the same text as matched by the 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '<'.
○ Match a character in the set [!/?A-Za-z].
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match ':'.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a character in the set [\t ].
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
○ Match the string "^^".

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.ComplexScripts.FindBothInFile(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Both answers of the scan in one pass: the first script that needs shaping stops the scan and wins the file; the first script rhwp cannot measure is remembered while the scan runs on. Only letters inside words count: a symbol or unit on its own (α, Ω, μm in a Korean report) draws fine, and rhwp, the most faithful renderer for Korean documents, keeps them. An extended Latin letter or combining mark counts next to any letter (Polish, Vietnamese words); a letter of another script only next to one of the same script (Отчёт, Αναφορά).
member.param: Format id of the file (docx, txt, hwpx, ...).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.EngineCaches.Release
member.summary: Drops what the engines cache between conversions; the next one looks everything up again. Meant for idle times, but safe while a conversion runs (the trim's busy check can't stop one from starting right after it): the caches only forget references, nothing still in use is disposed, and each thread disposes its own measuring fonts the next time it measures. NativeMemoryStressTests releases them during conversions.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.EngineDownloads.MirrorRoot
member.summary: Filee's own copy of every pinned download (Cloudflare R2 behind dl.filee.sh), filed under its SHA-256. A download site drops old versions (LibreOffice's "stable" folder lost 26.2.6 when 26.2.7 came out, #1474), and a released Filee can't change its pinned URL, so when the URL fails the installer takes the file from here. The pinned SHA-256 is checked either way, so a copy here can't be anything but the pinned file.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.EngineDownloads.IsSuggested(Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.EnginePackage)
member.summary: Ticked by default in the installer and in the first-run choice. Large downloads are offered, not suggested: LibreOffice is only needed for older formats (DOC, XLS, PPT, OpenDocument), FFmpeg (~100 MB) only for video and audio, calibre (~230 MB) only for rare e-book formats and Kindle output. Ghostscript and Tesseract are small but only needed for EPS / PostScript and for scans. WeasyPrint is small too, but changes how HTML, Markdown and e-mails become PDFs, so it is the user's choice (#1403).

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.ProcessRunner.StalledErrorKey
member.summary: The reason shown when a program stopped writing anything for the stall limit and was stopped.
Starts with the given arguments (no shell, arguments are escaped), waits for it to exit and kills the whole process tree on timeout or cancellation.
member.exception: Windows could not start the program because a DLL is missing (see ), or it stalled ().
The program did not exit within ; it was killed.
member.param: The longest the program may run; for no limit.
Called with every line of standard output and error as it arrives (e.g. to parse progress).

When set, the program is also killed once it has written nothing (no line on either stream) for this long: for engines that keep reporting progress, so a long run that does goes on and a hung one stops early.

Polled while the program runs (not together with ); once it has returned true on several polls in a row the program is killed and treated as finished (exit code 0). On Windows, a Job Object also ends the programs it started, even after it exited itself.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Infrastructure.ProcessRunner.RunWithOutputAsync(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String},System.Action{System.IO.Stream,System.Threading.CancellationToken},System.TimeSpan,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int64})
member.summary: Starts like , but hands its standard output to as bytes while it runs instead of collecting text (7-Zip's -so). When throws (it has read more than it takes), the program is killed and the exception passed on. The result's standard output is empty.
member.exception: The program did not exit within ; it was killed.
member.param: Where it runs; by default the folder it is in.

The most memory the program may use, in bytes, roughly. On Windows, the limit of a Job Object it and the programs it starts are in: what goes over fails to allocate. Elsewhere, or without a job, it is killed once its memory goes over (), which is looked at ten times a second, as nothing else limits memory on both Linux and macOS: it can get ahead by what it allocates in that time, and that doesn't count a program it started and didn't become.

member.summary: The whole of covered with an effect pixels large (a square's side or the blur's sigma): the window's preview, of which it shows the parts inside the frames.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.AreaHider.Pixelate(ImageMagick.IMagickImage{System.Byte},System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32},System.Double)
member.summary: Every pixel of becomes the average colour of its square on a grid of -pixel squares laid from the picture's top-left corner ().
member.remarks: Averaging is many-to-one: a square's worth of pixels becomes one colour, and what made it up is gone. Squares on the edge of a part are averaged over all of their pixels, those beside the part too (which stay in view anyway): the grid stays the same wherever a part is moved, and two parts that meet look like one. How large a square has to be to make text unreadable is 's concern.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.AreaHider.Box(ImageMagick.IMagickImage{System.Byte},System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32})
member.summary: filled with opaque black: every pixel of the part is replaced, transparency included, so nothing of it is left to recover.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.AreaHider.ClearExtraChannels(ImageMagick.IMagickImage{System.Byte},System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32})
member.summary: The channels a picture can carry beside its colours and alpha (a TIFF's extra samples, read as meta channels) set to 0 inside . Pixelate and Box write colours and alpha only, and what was under a part must not stay behind in them. Blur works on a copy of the picture, so it covers them with the rest.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.AreaHider.Blur(ImageMagick.IMagickImage{System.Byte},System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32},System.Double)
member.summary: blurred with a Gaussian of pixels, after its pixels are averaged into squares of about a third of it.
member.remarks: A light blur can be undone: it is a known convolution, and deconvolving it (sharpening with the inverse) brings back text whose strokes it only smeared. Here the part is first scaled down by averaging, which throws pixels away for good, and then blurred so widely (a sigma about a line of text, see ) that the detail of a letter is far below what an 8-bit pixel can hold. Pixels beside the part are blurred with it, so its edge doesn't show a seam, but only the part is written back.

member.name: T:Filee.Engines.Magick.BackgroundRemover
member.summary: Makes a plain (single-colour) background transparent. Built for signatures, stamps and logos on paper or a flat backdrop; photos of people, hair or busy scenes need a segmentation model and are out of scope.

remarks.para: 1. The backdrop colour is the per-channel median of the border pixels, which shrugs off ink touching the edge and JPEG noise. 2. A light backdrop is then estimated again per block, so a shadow or a lamp's falloff across a phone photo of paper is removed as well; a block only counts pixels that are a brighter or darker shade of the border colour, so a pale logo colour is not taken for paper. 3. Each pixel is treated as ink of some colour laid over the backdrop with some opacity (as GIMP's "Color to Alpha"): the opacity is how far the pixel is from the backdrop towards black or white, and the ink colour is recovered from it. Anti-aliased stroke edges therefore stay smooth and lose their white fringe instead of becoming a jagged cut-out. This only holds for a blend of backdrop and ink, which lies between the two: artwork in colours of its own (a drawing on a coloured backdrop) stays solid and unchanged, or un-mixing would turn it half transparent and shift its colours away from the backdrop's. 4. Lone visible pixels (noise, paper grain) are cleared.

Optionally only the backdrop reachable from the image edge is removed, so the white inside a logo stays. This is off by default because it would also keep the paper inside the loops of handwriting ("o", "a", "e").

member.summary: The raw opacity that counts as fully opaque: that of the ink itself (75th percentile of the clearly visible pixels, so the core of a stroke is solid and only its edges are not). Black ink reaches about 0.9 and its anti-aliased edges keep their partial alpha; faint pencil reaches only about 0.4, and its strokes still become solid instead of half transparent.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.BackgroundRemover.Blends(System.Byte[],System.Byte[],System.Int32,Filee.Engines.Magick.BackgroundRemover.Backdrop,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The partly opaque pixels that are a blend of the backdrop and an ink (an anti-aliased stroke edge, faint pencil, a shadow on the paper), which are un-mixed; the others are artwork in a colour of its own. A blend lies between the two: it grows more transparent towards removed backdrop, and more opaque towards ink of the colour it un-mixes to. Both are needed on a coloured backdrop, where every colour un-mixes to something: the blue body of a drawing on teal un-mixes to dark navy like its outline but lies past the outline, and a grey strip between two outlines that touches the backdrop at its end un-mixes to pink, which no ink next to it has. A shadow on the paper is a blend with no ink next to it: one un-mixing to a grey of an ink in the image still counts.

member.summary: Image formats ImageMagick can read (see for RAW, layered and metafile sources). Camera RAW is decoded by LibRaw; HEIC, DICOM, Photo CD, OpenEXR, Radiance HDR and FITS are read only. EMF/WMF are Windows metafiles, which ImageMagick renders through GDI+ on Windows only (). APNG is read and written by Filee's own (its frames decoded and encoded by ImageMagick); FITS is read by Filee's own and written to TIFF by . ANI (an animated cursor) is read by Filee's own , its frames decoded by ImageMagick. GIMP's XCF is read and written by Filee's own and .

member.summary: Formats whose frames are an animation; an AVIF only when it is an image sequence (), and an animated cursor (), read only. Between these, all frames are kept with their timing (an animated GIF becomes an animated WebP, JPEG XL or AVIF and the other way round); any other target gets the first frame.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Magick.ImageEncoder.Edge(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The edge an image engine offers from a picture in to . GIF holds 256 colours, so a still picture costs more there: it reaches video through a full-colour PNG instead (FFmpeg), while animations and multi-page files still go through GIF and keep their frames. Still picture → APNG costs as much, so photos never reach video as a one-frame animation. FITS → TIFF is the data for further processing (linear by default, 16 or 32 bits): it costs a little more, so FITS reaches other formats through a stretched PNG or JPG instead.

HEIC could carry alpha as an auxiliary picture; Filee's writer (Heic/HeicWriter) does not. XBM and WBMP are 1-bit, PFM has no alpha, and the alpha planes of PCX and Sun Raster are an ImageMagick extension other programs ignore (its palette writers drop them altogether).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.ClipPreview.SilenceLine
member.remarks:
Pattern:
silence_(start|end):\\s*(-?[0-9.]+(?:e-?[0-9]+)?)
Explanation:
○ Match the string "silence_".
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "start".
○ Match the string "end".
○ Match ':'.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '-' atomically, optionally.
○ Match a character in the set [.0-9] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match 'e'.
○ Match '-' atomically, optionally.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.FfmpegConverter.BuildEdges
member.summary: Every video format (read by FFmpeg's demuxers) → every video target, animated GIF or APNG, a still PNG frame, every frame as PNG or JPG pictures (only when a preset asks for it, see ), every audio target and SRT / ASS / WebVTT (its subtitles); every audio format → every audio target (including itself: re-encode with another bitrate); GIF, APNG and PNG → MP4, WEBM, MOV; every image ImageMagick reads → HEIC. Only formats the pinned build can write are targets (see MediaEncoding).
member.remarks: The GIF and APNG edges cost more (slow, large), so video → JPG / PDF / TIFF … goes through the still frame (video → PNG → image engines) and never renders an animation of a whole film just to take one frame of it. The other way, a photo (HEIC, JPG, …) reaches video as a full-colour PNG: the image engines' still → GIF and still → APNG edges cost 12 (), so 10 + 11 beats 12 + 10 and 12 + 11. Animated GIF/WebP and PDF or TIFF pages keep the GIF route (10 + 10, APNG costs 10 + 11), which keeps their frames; an APNG goes straight to video.

member.summary: The size limit (#553), after the capped encode: usually it fits. A bitrate is an average, so when it missed, the video is encoded once more at a bitrate as much lower as it missed by, on the rest of the progress bar. Refuses when that still doesn't fit (or the length is unknown), rather than hand over a file too large.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.FfmpegConverter.StagedOutput.#ctor(Filee.Core.Conversion.IOutputAllocator,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Hands out paths in the work directory for outputs whose real path comes from . That one is never : with "overwrite", IMG_0001.HEIC → MOV would otherwise be written over IMG_0001.MOV, the Live Photo's own video, so it gets a numbered name instead.

Runs , planned with . When a hardware encode fails (a driver error, a picture larger than the chip encodes, …) the file is encoded again as plans it without hardware: an encoder that passed its test encode can still refuse one particular video, and the user asked for a converted file, not for the GPU. The failure is logged, not reported. Cancellation is never retried.

Cancellation and failures that are about the output, not the subtitles (), are not retried.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.FfmpegConverter.VersionPattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
version\\s+n?(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)+|\\S+)
Explanation:
○ Match the string "version".
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Match 'n' greedily, optionally.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Loop greedily and atomically at least once.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match any character other than a whitespace character atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.FfmpegConverter.DemuxerLine
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^ D[E. ]?[d. ]? +(?<names>[a-z0-9_][\\w,.-]*)
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string " D".
○ Match a character in the set [ .E] greedily, optionally.
○ Match a character in the set [ .d] greedily, optionally.
○ Match ' ' atomically at least once.
○ "names" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [,-.\w] atomically any number of times.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.Candidates(System.String,Filee.Engines.Media.HostPlatform,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String},System.Boolean)
member.summary: The hardware encoders for ("h264", "hevc" or "av1") worth trying, best first. Windows: NVIDIA, then Intel, then AMD (a laptop with an Intel chip and an NVIDIA card encodes on the card). macOS: VideoToolbox with constant quality (Apple Silicon), then with a bitrate (Intel Macs); none for AV1, which VideoToolbox can't encode. Linux: NVIDIA, then VA-API when a render node exists. Only encoders the FFmpeg in use lists are tried (all of them when the list could not be read); the probe decides which one really works, so a chip too old for AV1 (before the RTX 40 series, Arc and Core Ultra, RDNA 3) leaves AV1 to SVT-AV1.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.TenBit(System.String,Filee.Engines.Media.VideoStreamInfo)
member.summary: True when the video is encoded in 10 bits: HEVC and AV1 keep 10-bit and HDR sources in 10 bits (HEVC Main 10, AV1 Main), as x265 and SVT-AV1 do. H.264 is always 8-bit 4:2:0, the only format every player decodes (as with x264).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.Quantizer(System.String,Filee.Core.Presets.MediaQuality)
member.summary: The preset's quality on the encoders' 0–51 quantizer scale (NVENC -cq, Quick Sync -global_quality, AMF and VA-API -qp): one above x264's CRF 18/23/28 for H.264 and x265's 22/26/30 for HEVC. Hardware encoders lack x264/x265's psychovisual tuning and spend bits less wisely, so the same number gives a larger file; one step coarser keeps the size close at a slightly lower quality. AV1 gets HEVC's numbers: only Quick Sync takes this scale for AV1 (its ICQ is 1–51 for every codec, 26 by default as for HEVC).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.Av1Quantizer(Filee.Core.Presets.MediaQuality)
member.summary: The preset's quality on AV1's 0–63 quantizer scale (NVENC -cq), the scale of SVT-AV1's CRF: two above its 26/32/40, about the one step coarser H.264 and HEVC get, on AV1's finer scale.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.Av1QIndex(Filee.Core.Presets.MediaQuality)
member.summary: on AV1's 0–255 quantizer index (base_q_idx), which AMF (-qp_p) and VA-API (-global_quality) take: quantizer q is index 4q, as AV1 encoders map their CRF.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.HardwareVideo.VideoToolboxQuality(Filee.Core.Presets.MediaQuality)
member.summary: VideoToolbox's constant quality (-q:v, 1–100, higher is better) on Apple Silicon.

○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match ':'.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '-' atomically, optionally.

○ Match ':'.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.SplitCopy(System.String,System.String,System.String,Filee.Core.Presets.MediaOptions,Filee.Engines.Media.MediaInfo)
member.summary: The whole video in parts (#1259), copied as it is like : FFmpeg's segment muxer writes them as (part%04d.mp4), each starting at 0. A copy can only break at a key frame, so a part ends at the first one at or after its point (): parts never overlap and nothing is encoded, but one may be a few seconds longer than asked, and a video with few key frames gives fewer parts.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.AnimatedGif(System.String,System.String,Filee.Core.Presets.MediaOptions,Filee.Engines.Media.MediaInfo,System.String,System.Double)
member.summary: Animated GIF in two passes: the first finds the 256 colours that suit the whole clip best (palettegen), the second maps every frame to them (paletteuse). A single pass with a fixed palette looks banded; generating the palette in the same run would keep every frame in memory until the end. Frame rate and width are limited by the quality setting because GIF stores every frame uncompressed-ish and grows fast.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.AnimatedPng(System.String,System.String,Filee.Core.Presets.MediaOptions,Filee.Engines.Media.MediaInfo,System.Double)
member.summary: Animated PNG with FFmpeg's APNG encoder and muxer: full colour (24-bit RGB, no palette pass), looping, with the frame rate and width limits of GIF, since every frame is stored losslessly.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.GifFrames(Filee.Engines.Media.VideoStreamInfo,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double)
member.summary: Playback speed, frame rate, square pixels and size of the GIF frames (never upscaled). The speed changes the timestamps before the frame rate is taken, so a faster clip keeps the frame rate by leaving frames out, and a slower one repeats frames where the video has too few.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.SquarePixels(Filee.Engines.Media.VideoStreamInfo)
member.summary: Images have no pixel aspect ratio: anamorphic video (DV, DVD) is stretched to square pixels first.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.PosterFrame(System.String,System.String,Filee.Engines.Media.MediaInfo)
member.summary: One full-size PNG frame from a tenth into the video (the first frames are often black), the start for video → image conversions (the image engines take it from there). Without this edge the route planner would reach images through an animated GIF of the whole video.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Media.MediaEncoding.PlanStill(System.String,System.String,System.String,Filee.Core.Presets.MediaOptions,Filee.Engines.Media.MediaInfo)
member.summary: A video that shows the PNG for . The image engines write that PNG at full size and colour, so pictures never pass through a 256-colour GIF on their way to video.
member.remarks: The PNG's ICC profile or colour chunks give the primaries and transfer (a Display P3 photo stays P3 in the video); RGB becomes BT.709 YUV in TV range, tagged as such. Transparent areas turn black, like the bars around a video. 30 frames per second play everywhere; identical frames cost x264 (tuned for stills) and VP9 almost nothing, so the quality is one step above the preset's (Balanced encodes like High): the file is about the size of one picture either way.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.ReadOutputLimit
member.summary: The most a read may print, the file's own text: a TIFF can hold a long description. The richest of ExifTool's own sample files prints 26 KB, as large binary values print as a note of their size, but a compressed PNG text chunk prints a thousand times the size of the file.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.ReadMemoryLimit

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.EditableFamilies
member.summary: Families whose fields are written into the file and can be changed. The others describe the file or are worked out from it (File, System, Composite, ExifTool), or are kept whole: maker notes, colour profiles, Photoshop's resources, JFIF.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.ReadOnlyGroups

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.ReadOnlyTags

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.IfdFields

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.PdfFields

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.PngFields

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.ListFields

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.LocationTags
member.summary: What Remove location takes out at once, whole groups and structures among it; the fields it finds in the file () go by name as well.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.NotInTheFile

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.IsLocation(Filee.Engines.Metadata.MetadataField)
member.summary: A field that says where the file was made: what Remove location takes of the editable fields, what the window strikes through for it and what must be gone from the copy. Any spelling of GPS (a drone's "GpsLatitude"), any name with Location or Altitude in it (a video's "LocationInformation", XMP's "LocationCreatedCity"), and the address fields. A field that can't be edited stays, in plain sight (a camera's "FocusLocation" is no place).

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Metadata.ExifTool.LocationOutOfReach(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Filee.Engines.Metadata.MetadataField})
member.summary: The place fields out of reach of Remove location, each once: a camera's maker notes (Panasonic's City), another block kept whole (a C2PA manifest's ExifGPSLatitude), a PNG's or a PDF's own field, a GeoTIFF's map position, named once for the directory that holds it. ExifTool can't take them one by one, and they stay in plain sight. An empty one, or Panasonic's "---", says no place.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.HasResolution(System.String)
member.summary: True when the picture says how large it is meant to be. Without that Tesseract guesses 70 dpi (a page of a metre and more); 300 dpi is what scanners write.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.SmallSide
member.summary: A picture whose short side is under this many pixels is enlarged before recognition. Tesseract reads text best when its letters are about 20–30 pixels tall (its guidance: accuracy drops below 10 pt at 300 dpi, rapidly below 8 pt). Screenshots and pictures saved from the web are made at screen resolution, where body text is 10–16 pixels tall (#138: a 658 × 789 screenshot with Chinese characters a dozen pixels high). An A4 or Letter page scanned at 150 dpi or more is at least 1240 pixels on its short side, so a picture smaller than this is a screenshot, a crop, a small page or a scan below 120 dpi: small text, in nearly every case.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.EnlargeBy
member.summary: Small pictures are read at twice their size: letters of 10–16 pixels become 20–32.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.MaxEnlargedPixels
member.summary: The enlarged copy has at most this many pixels: about 100 MB as Tesseract holds it (32 bits a pixel), a little more than an A3 page at 300 dpi (17 megapixels). A long, narrow screenshot is enlarged less, or not at all.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.LeastEnlargement
member.summary: Enlarging by less than this changes too little to be worth a copy of the picture.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Ocr.TesseractConverter.EnlargeFactor(System.UInt32,System.UInt32,System.Nullable{System.Double})

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Office.LinkedContent.Scheme
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\\-]*:
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Za-z].
○ Match a character in the set [+-.0-9A-Za-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match ':'.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Office.LinkedContent.Tag
member.remarks:
Pattern:
<(?<name>[A-Za-z][\\w:.\\-]*)(?<attributes>(?:\\s+[^\\s=>/]+(?:\\s*=\\s*(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^\\s>]+))?)*)(?<end>\\s*/?)>
Explanation:
○ Match '<'.
○ "name" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Za-z].
○ Match a character in the set [-.:\w] greedily any number of times.
○ "attributes" capture group.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [^/=>\s] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match '='.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '"'.
○ Match a character other than '"' atomically any number of times.
○ Match '"'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '\''.
○ Match a character other than '\'' atomically any number of times.
○ Match '\''.
○ Match a character in the set [^>\s] greedily at least once.
○ "end" capture group.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match '/' atomically, optionally.
○ Match '>'.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Office.PandocConverter.PlainMarkdown
member.summary:
Keeps the Markdown free of HTML, which many Markdown editors show as code (#391). GitHub-flavoured Markdown tables have one header row, one line per cell and no merged cells, and Pandoc writes any other table as HTML: this lays every table out as a plain grid instead. A merged cell keeps its text in its first position and leaves the others empty, the paragraphs and list items of a cell are joined with
, and a table without a header row gets its first row as the header. Pictures lose their Word size, which only an can hold.

○ Optional (greedy).
○ "currency" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [$\u00A3\u00A5\u20A9\u20AC\u20B9].
○ "whole" capture group.

member.summary: True when every byte decodes as CP949 without a substitute. Western text fails here (an accented letter followed by a space or punctuation is no CP949 pair), so a Korean PC still reads a Windows-1252 file as Windows-1252.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Subtitles.SubtitleEncoding.Declared(System.Byte[])
member.summary: The encoding named by charset=… (SAMI's HTML) or encoding="…" (XML) near the start.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Subtitles.SubtitleEncoding.LooksKorean(System.Byte[])
member.summary: True when the non-ASCII bytes form CP949 pairs, most of them Hangul syllables of KS X 1001 (lead byte B0–C8, trail byte A1–FE) and hardly any with a lead byte above C8, as Korean text is. Western text decoded as CP949 gives pairs with ASCII trail bytes; Chinese GBK text uses lead bytes above C8 for a good part of its common characters (的 B5C4 but 是 CAC7, 我 CED2, 这 D5E2), where Korean has only the rare Hanja.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Translation.KeyedTranslation.TranslateAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.String,System.String,Filee.Engines.Translation.ITranslationService,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Translates in one keyed request and recovers partial answers: the texts that came back are kept and only the missing ones are asked for again — one keyed request per round, in slot order, up to . An answer with no visible text counts as a miss, so a text is never emptied by a stray marker, and if a text comes back twice, the first answer stays. Returns one trimmed, marker-free entry per text; null means it never came back and the caller applies its own fallback.
member.param: Between the markers. Subtitle cues are lines of their own ("\n"); the runs of a paragraph are pieces of one sentence, cut wherever the formatting changes, so they go joined (""), and the model reads the whole sentence instead of translating each piece as a line, which matters for languages that reorder it.

member.name: T:Filee.Engines.Translation.OllamaEndpoint
member.summary: Where Filee reaches the local Ollama server. Ollama reads its own OLLAMA_HOST variable to listen on another port or address, so Filee reads the same variable. It follows it only while it names this computer: the translator sends the whole document text to Ollama, and a remote host would carry it off the machine.

member.summary: The server's base address, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434. Read once per run, like Ollama does.

member.summary: The base address as shown to the user, without a trailing slash.

member.name: P:Filee.Engines.Translation.OllamaEndpoint.IgnoredValue

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Translation.OllamaEndpoint.Resolve(System.String)
member.summary: The base address for an OLLAMA_HOST value, and the value itself when it was refused.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Translation.OllamaEndpoint.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Reads an OLLAMA_HOST value the way Ollama does: host, host:port, :port or http(s)://host:port, with port 11434 when neither a port nor a scheme is given. Returns null for a host that isn't this computer or a value that can't be read. An empty host, 0.0.0.0 or :: means Ollama listens on every interface, which includes loopback, so Filee connects through loopback.

member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(#{1,6}\\s+|[-*+]\\s+(\\[[ xX]\\]\\s+)?|\\d+[.)]\\s+|>\\s*)+
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Loop greedily and atomically at least once.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 4 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '#' atomically at least 1 and at most 6 times.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [*+-].
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match '['.
○ Match a character in the set [ Xx].
○ Match ']'.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a character in the set [).].
○ Match a whitespace character greedily at least once.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '>'.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Canvas.CanvasMarkdown.WikiLink
member.remarks:
Pattern:
!?\\[\\[(?<target>[^\\[\\]|]+)(?:\\|(?<alias>[^\\[\\]]+))?\\]\\]
Explanation:
○ Match '!' atomically, optionally.
○ Match the string "[[".
○ "target" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [^[]|] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match '|'.
○ "alias" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [^[]] greedily at least once.
○ Match the string "]]".

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Canvas.CanvasMarkdown.MarkdownLink
member.remarks:
Pattern:
!?\\[([^\\]]*)\\]\\([^)]*\\)
Explanation:
○ Match '!' atomically, optionally.
○ Match '['.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character other than ']' atomically any number of times.
○ Match the string "](".
○ Match a character other than ')' atomically any number of times.
○ Match ')'.

○ Zero-width positive lookahead.

○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Zero-width positive lookbehind.
○ Match any character other than a whitespace character right-to-left.
○ Match a character in the set [*_].
○ Zero-width negative lookahead.
○ Match a word character.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberReader.FormatDigits
member.remarks:
Pattern:
X(\\d)(\\d)Y(\\d)(\\d)
Explanation:
○ Match 'X'.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit.
○ Match 'Y'.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberReader.ApertureDefinition
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^ADD(\\d+)([^,]+)(?:,(.*))?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "ADD".
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a character other than ',' greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match ','.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberReader.BlockStart
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^ABD(\\d+)$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "ABD".
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberReader.StepRepeat
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^SRX(\\d+)Y(\\d+)(?:I([-+\\d.]+))?(?:J([-+\\d.]+))?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "SRX".
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match 'Y'.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match 'I'.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+-.\d] greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match 'J'.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+-.\d] greedily at least once.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberSvg.Subtract(System.Collections.Generic.List{Filee.Engines.Vector.Gerber.GerberObject},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The dark objects with every later clear object that overlaps them subtracted, the clear objects dropped. Only what stays clear is subtracted: a clear object minus the dark objects drawn after it. A hole that a later object fills again would otherwise meet it edge to edge, and anti-aliasing would show the background along that edge. Past the budget (or if Skia can't resolve an outline) the objects are returned as they are, clear ones included.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.GhostscriptConverter.ConvertToPdfAAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rewrites a PDF as PDF/A-2b. Colours become RGB to match the sRGB output intent the standard asks for, fonts are embedded, and what PDF/A doesn't allow is left out rather than the file refused (policy 1). A tagged PDF loses its tags (pdfwrite doesn't carry them), which part B doesn't need. Ghostscript reads a copy whose visible annotations print (): PDF/A leaves out every annotation that doesn't.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.GhostscriptConverter.OutputIntent(System.Byte[])
member.summary: The PostScript that gives the PDF its output intent, as Ghostscript's PDFA_def.ps does: without it pdfwrite marks the file PDF/A but leaves the intent out. The profile goes in as a hex string, not as a file the script reads, so safe mode needn't open a path and a folder name with brackets or non-ASCII letters can't break the script.

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.GhostscriptConverter.DeclaresPdfA(System.String)

member.name: M:Filee.Engines.Vector.GhostscriptConverter.RenderCmykAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Int32},System.Int32,System.Byte[],System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.IProgress{System.Double})
member.summary: Renders PDF pages to 8-bit CMYK TIFFs (tiff32nc), one per page in page order, for , which renders RGB only. DeviceCMYK colours keep the numbers the document gives them: Ghostscript's default CMYK profile is both their source and the output, so nothing is converted. With (the document's CMYK output intent) that profile takes both places instead, and RGB or ICC-based content is converted into it. Pages are cut to the crop box, as PDFium does.
member.param: Zero-based pages, or null for every page.

Pattern:
&(?:(?<number>#[0-9]+;|#[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]+;)|(?<name>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*);)?
Explanation:
○ Match '&'.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ "number" capture group.
○ Match '#'.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9] atomically at least once.
○ Match ';'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Xx].
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Fa-f] atomically at least once.
○ Match ';'.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ "name" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Z_a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [-.0-9A-Z_a-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match ';'.

member.summary: SVG, SVGZ and AI conversions and raster image tracing that need no external program.

member.name: F:Filee.Engines.Vector.VectorConverter.TraceCost
member.summary: Cost of tracing a raster image into SVG. Tracing redraws the picture, so it must never be a step on the way to another format (PNG → SVG → PDF instead of PNG → PDF): its cost is higher than any route from an image to a format SVG leads to, and the planner only takes it when SVG (or DXF, DWG through SVG) is the target. Its edges are for raster sources only: a PDF, EPS or other vector file that can be rendered to PNG is never traced.

member.summary: Releases this caller's reference to a COM object now instead of when the garbage collector gets to it (a decoder keeps its file open).
